title: Noah's cedars (Tanchuma Noach 5)
hook: Noah planted and cut cedars for years so people would ask why, and turn
tomorrow: a palace in flames, nobody in sight. who's in charge?

segments.voice: That was a week of building: the blueprint, this one pleases me, truth from the earth, even the urge, don't ruin my world. And yesterday's line: one family. Today, a builder who wanted his neighbors to ask.

Some things get a question every time: a tattoo, a bracelet you never take off, a mezuzah on a doorpost. People ask, what's that? Midrash Tanchuma imagines Noah doing that on purpose. Before the flood, it says, he didn't just build. He planted cedar trees, and then he cut them down.
screen: `WHAT'S THAT?` → `NOAH PLANTS CEDARS.` → `AND CUTS THEM DOWN.`

segments.voice: People kept walking by. What are these cedars for? And Noah answered: the Master of the world is bringing a flood, and told me to make an ark. In the midrash, the question was the point. Every cedar was an invitation to ask, and every answer was a chance to turn. They mocked him instead. That changes the story. In this telling the flood isn't an ambush. There was time, and a man in the open with saws and seedlings, answering anyone who asked. Noah kept planting anyway. They could have asked, and listened. Now the week, back as one picture. A plan drawn before the building. A world chosen, not perfect. Truth planted in the ground. An urge that builds houses. A garden on loan. One family. And a builder whose slow work was a question left open for his neighbors.
screen: `PLANT, THEN CUT.` · `EVERY CEDAR, A QUESTION.` · `THEY MOCKED HIM INSTEAD.` · `A WEEK OF BUILDING.` · then, large: `THEY COULD HAVE ASKED.`

segments.voice: Choose one thing you do that someone might ask about: a blessing before food, a candle on Friday night, a habit you keep. In one or two sentences, say out loud how you'd answer if a stranger asked why. Keep it plain and warm, then sit with the quiet after.
Noah's cedars: in Midrash Tanchuma, trees planted and cut in the open, so people would ask why and have the chance to turn.
For the road: they could have asked, and the cedars kept the question open. Day fifteen seventy-five, a week built.

screen: `DAY 1575 COUNTS.` → `READING MIDRASH · 8 OF 40.` → `TOMORROW: A PALACE IN FLAMES, NOBODY IN SIGHT. WHO'S IN CHARGE?`

howItsDone: Midrash Tanchuma is read alongside the weekly Torah portion; this passage belongs to Noach, the portion of the flood, read in synagogues in the fall.
